source.title: Great white shark
source.quote: Females weigh 1,000–1,900 kg (2,200–4,200 lb) while males weigh 680–1,000 kg (1,500–2,200 lb).

mass_kg.note: Adult females. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

source.title: Great white shark
source.quote: Female white sharks are mature at 4.6–4.9 m (15–16 ft) while males are mature at 3.4–4.0 m (11–13 ft).

size_m.note: Length of a mature female. Upper end of the stated range; the source gives no mean.

source.title: Great white shark
source.quote: White sharks are estimated to swim 2.88–4.86 km/h (1.79–3.02 mph) but can sprint up to 24.12 km/h (14.99 mph).

top_speed_mps.note: Converted from the 24.12 km/h sprint; range is the standard +/-10%.

source.title: Great white shark
source.quote: From this, the researchers calculated that a specimen 6.4 m (21 ft) long and weighing 3,324 kg (7,328 lb) could exert a bite force of 9,320 newtons (2,100 lbf) in the front and 18,216 newtons (4,095 lbf) in the back.

attack_force_n.note: Front bite the 2008 CT-scan study calculated for a 6.4 m, 3,324 kg shark, heavier than the adult female here, so it is on the high side; range is the standard +/-10%.

attacks_per_s.note: No published attack rate found for this animal; category default.

reach_m.note: reach = 0.25 x size_m (lunging bite), from size_m.

armor_0_1.note: armor level 2: thick, tough skin covered in denticles.

endurance_s.note: No source gives how long it can keep fighting; category default.

aggression_0_1.note: aggression level 4: apex predator, confident against most animals.

group_tactics_0_1.note: group tactics level 1: solitary, fights alone.
